If Android will not let you allow SMS (Android 13 and newer, app installed outside a store):
1. Open Settings › Apps › GeekBridge (the button above).
2. Tap the ⋮ menu at the top right › Allow restricted settings, and confirm with your screen lock.
3. Come back, switch on Messages and tap Allow for SMS (or Settings › Apps › GeekBridge › Permissions › SMS › Allow).

GeekBridge does not need to be your default SMS app and never asks to be. It reads the SMS store and sends plain texts. Picture messages (MMS) and RCS chats stay in your messaging app, and marking a message read on the computer does not mark it read on the phone.
All set. You can change this later in app settings.
Android will not show the question again. Switch it on in app settings: Permissions › %1$s.
Optional: GeekBridge works without it; the related feature stays off.
Recommended. You can link without it, but alerts and the background connection notice will not show.
Tells you when a linked computer asks this phone to place a call, and asks first if you chose that.
Ask me before placing a call for a computer
Always shown on the phone as “Dialing … requested by …”, and a computer can place only a few calls per 10 minutes. Turn this on to also approve each call here.
Share call status with my computer
Linked computers you allow “Calls” for see ringing and in-call, and can answer, decline or end.
Off by default. If you allow it, a computer you linked and allowed “Calls” for can ask this phone to dial a number. Android asks for the Phone permission only when you tap below.
Allow placing calls from my computer
Allowed. A linked computer you allowed “Calls” for can ask this phone to dial a number. Switch “Ask me before placing a call” on to approve each call here too.

Call audio does not travel through GeekBridge. It stays on the phone unless your computer is also paired with this phone over Bluetooth as a hands-free device. Needs the Phone state step; declining and ending a call needs Android 9 or newer.

To talk through your computer’s headphones and microphone, pair this phone with the computer over Bluetooth. On the computer: add device, then choose this phone. On this phone, allow Phone calls access (One UI: Bluetooth, the gear next to the computer, Call audio on). Android gives apps no call audio, so this is the only way.
Pair phone with your computer for call audio

To tell you whether your computer is connected for call audio, Android needs to let GeekBridge see which Bluetooth devices are connected. GeekBridge only lists connected devices; it never scans for new ones.

You chose not to allow this, so Android may still pause GeekBridge with the screen off. You can try again, or change it in the app\u2019s settings.

Background use is restricted for GeekBridge, so the connection to your computer will not stay up with the screen off. Open the battery settings below and choose “Unrestricted” (or “Allow background usage”).

resources.string: Link this phone with your computer once. After that they find each other on your network automatically, and nothing is trusted until you confirm a matching code.
Lets GeekBridge show a quiet notice while it stays connected, and tell you about incoming files.

Lets this phone show names instead of numbers for calls and messages, and, if you share contacts, fills the Contacts app on your computer. Nothing leaves this phone unless you switch on Share contacts.

Lets you share your calendars (including Google Calendar accounts that sync on this phone) with the Calendar app on your computer. Read-only; the computer can only add or change events if you separately switch on editing later, in Share with computer.
Lets GeekBridge know whether the phone is idle, ringing or in a call. It never sees phone numbers or call history.

Lets a linked computer you trust answer, decline or end a call on this phone, so a ringing call can be handled from your desk. You can also let it start a call from this phone. GeekBridge cannot hear the call: audio stays on the phone unless the computer is also its Bluetooth hands-free device.

Shows who is calling on your computer. Android gives an app a caller\'s number only with the “Call logs” permission, so GeekBridge asks for it; the call log itself is never read or sent. Allow Contacts too to see the name. Without it, or for a hidden number, the computer says “Unknown caller”.
Your computer shows the caller\'s number when Android provides it.
Your computer can\'t show who is calling, only that a call is ringing. Allow Call logs to show the number.

Optionally share your battery level, phone notifications, contacts, calendar and text messages with a linked computer. Each part needs its own Android permission. Text messages are limited by Android and Google Play; the notes below explain how.
Keeps the connection to your computer alive when the screen is off. Without this, Android may pause GeekBridge and files or clipboard may arrive late.
Open GeekBridge on your computer, on the same Wi-Fi network as this phone, then look for it.
To stop trusting a computer, tap Unlink next to it.
To add another computer, open GeekBridge on it, on the same Wi-Fi network, then look for it.
Looking for computers on this network… keep GeekBridge open on the computer. Nothing showing up? Check that both devices use the same Wi-Fi and that a guest or VPN network is not in the way.
